references.text: The parallel in Matthew's version of the Lord's Prayer, where Jesus prays 'forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil'.
Jesus elaborates on the principle of forgiveness: if you forgive people their wrongdoings, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father forgive you.
The parable of the unmerciful servant illustrates the principle that we must forgive others as God forgives us – the same principle found in 'for we also forgive everyone who owes us'.
Jesus teaches that when you stand praying, you must forgive if you have anything against someone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.
Paul urges believers to forgive one another, just as God forgave you in Christ – an echo of the prayer's principle of mutual forgiveness.
The exhortation to bear with one another and forgive one another, just as the Lord has forgiven you, reflects the principle in Luke 11:4 that forgiveness is received and passed on.
James writes that God does not tempt anyone – this sheds light on the prayer 'lead us not into temptation' and its theological content regarding the origin of temptation.
God is faithful and will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, but with the temptation He will also provide a way out – related to the prayer not to be led into temptation.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials – this confirms that God can protect believers from temptation, as the prayer asks.
David's prayer for forgiveness in Psalm 51 – 'Be merciful to me, O God' – reflects the same humble attitude found in the prayer 'forgive us our sins'.
'Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven and whose sin is covered' – expresses the blessing of the forgiveness that the prayer in Luke 11:4 asks for.
Agur's prayer contains elements similar to the Lord's Prayer: a request to be kept from temptation and to receive what is necessary – a parallel to Luke 11:3-4.
Jesus says to the disciples in Gethsemane, 'Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation' – directly linked to the prayer not to be led into temptation.
